newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INCE SAYS WILL DECIDE FUTURE THIS MONTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INCE SAYS WILL DECIDE FUTURE THIS MONTH.

text.p: England midfielder Paul Ince, who scored two goals in Inter's 3-0 league win at Piacenza on Saturday, will decide on his future in two weeks time.
"I will decide my club for next season within the next two weeks," he told reporters at Inter's training ground on Sunday.

Ince, who picked up a booking on Saturday that will sideline him from Inter's important league match next weekend against Juventus, has a contract until 1998 but has been repeatedly linked with English clubs recently.

The 29-year-old player, in his second season at Inter after joining from Manchester United in 1995, has become a firm favourite of the local fans after a difficult start and has now scored six goals in 14 league matches this season.
On Saturday he leaped an advertising hoarding and kissed his shirt in front of the fans after scoring.
"Everybody continues to say that I will join Arsenal, Chelsea and Blackburn," Ince said.
"Yesterday, more than anything, I wanted to show that I want to win something with Inter."
Inter were beaten in the semifinals of the Italian Cup by Napoli on Wednesday and are seven points behind league leaders Juventus in the domestic league.
However they still have a chance of UEFA Cup glory and play Anderlecht in Brussels on Wednesday in the first leg of that competition's quarter-final stage.
